propertyEvents.locator: PDF pages 1 to 5; the vendor invoices the search selected: dates, service period and amounts

propertyEvents.result: All 10 payables invoices dated June 20 to 30 are for June work and are in the June books. Of the 5 invoices dated after June 30 the search selected, 4 are for June work and all four missed the year: Sound Ridge, Pellham & Quist and the two June utility bills, received July 8 to 17. Cobalt’s pay application 12, $1,342,880.00 for July, is rightly in July. The cut-off fails in one direction only: bills that arrive after the close are booked when they arrive.

Accruals and Interest
Set each accrual tested against the bills that followed
propertyEvents.locator: AP Aging!A8:F22 and Accrued Liabilities!A8:C15; payables by vendor and invoice, and every accrual with its basis

propertyEvents.result: The utilities accrual, $6,200.00, was May’s yard and office bill; it left out the temporary site power billed monthly in arrears. June’s actual bills came to $15,640.00: Northsound $4,980.00 and Cascadia $10,660.00. The accrual is short $9,440.00 (UL-03), under clearly trivial on its own but a known misstatement all the same. The workers’ compensation premium audit accrual, $42,000.00, covers the final bill of $39,850.00 with $2,150.00 to spare.

propertyEvents.result: Known misstatements add up to $247,985.00 of liabilities and expense: 97.2% of the $255,000.00 performance materiality and 72.9% of materiality. Sound Ridge’s cost also moves Pier 9 further along: at cost-to-cost it would add $204,835.16 of revenue, so its net effect on income is $18,435.16, which the CPA settles with the job schedule testing (CROSS-01). Close to performance materiality, the CPA weighs these with the other FY2026 areas. The machine stops here.
